item.title: AgentDesk: The System Behind the Scalable Backends Series
item.description:
Every post in the Scalable Backends series threads through one system instead of a dozen disconnected toy examples: AgentDesk, a fictional platform where customer teams deploy AI agents that handle customer chats, call external tools, run long sessions, and spin up sub-agents for parallel research. It’s scaling from roughly 100 to 100,000 concurrent sessions — which is exactly the kind of growth that forces every decision below.

This post is the reference diagram the rest of the series points back to. Click any box for details — ownership, technology, and design notes.

item.title: From Surviving to Becoming
item.description:
For the longest time I believed that strength meant enduring quietly. I thought love meant sacrifice, even when it slowly dimmed my light.

I smiled through physical pain when sepsis nearly took my life, when fibromyalgia made every day heavy, and when migraines stole my clarity. I thought carrying these emotional burdens which I didn’t even fully understand is what life is supposed to be like.

item.title: Technical Analysis: IRREGULAR, Containment Failure, and What It Means for Agent Governance
item.description:
If your eval can reach the open internet, it is not an eval. It is unsupervised deployment with better branding.

IRREGULAR sits in a weird place in the stack. Frontier labs hire it to run pre-deployment cyber evaluations: CTF-style scenarios, simulated corporate networks, multi-stage attack paths. The point is to measure whether a model can plan and execute real offensive campaigns before release. That work only works if the environment looks realistic. It also only works if “realistic” never becomes “actual production internet.”

item.title: Sense of Self: The Three Versions That Mess Us Up
item.description:
Okay, so I’ve been sitting with this idea for a bit now, raw thoughts spilling out like they always do. No neat structure, no fancy psychology jargon unless it fits, just me processing this out loud.

Sense of self: That slippery thing we all carry around but rarely stop to name properly.

There are three versions, at least the way I see it right now.

One: The “It’s All About Me” Version

My entity. My reactions. My benefits. My comfort. My whatever.

item.title: From Shattered to Unbreakable: How Resiliency Turned My Pain into Power
item.description:
Life has a way of testing the waters, making us uncomfortable enough to push and push further enough until we break. There is only one direction left after being down that much, going up.

My path has been full of these tests and you know what I gained? I gained how to be resilient in all the adversities. I learnt how to turn this pain into power. I learnt how to convert my limitations into breakthroughs. Here is my story, coming straight to you without any fluff … the real authentic flow of my life’s stormy waters that unlocked the most powerful version of myself.

item.description:

item.title: OpenClaw: Full Danger Edition
item.description:
OpenClaw is your local AI assistant that stays completely on your device with no cloud dependency. It runs on any operating system and platform, giving you full control without corporate oversight. Here is the unfiltered breakdown.

Architecture (how it actually flows)

Messaging Channels
(WhatsApp • Telegram • Slack • Discord • Signal • iMessage • Teams • Matrix • Google Chat • BlueBubbles • Zalo • WebChat…)
 ↓
┌───────────────┐
│ Gateway │ ← ws://127.0.0.1:18789
│ │ sessions • presence • cron • config • tool router • webhook hooks
└───────┬───────┘
 │
 ┌────┼────┐
 │ │ │
Pi/RPC CLI UI / Apps
Agent openclaw ├─ WebChat (browser lifeline)
 ├─ Control UI (admin dashboard)
 ├─ macOS menu bar (quick dopamine)
 └─ iOS / Android nodes (mobile eyes & ears)

 │
 ├─→ Tools (deep system reach)
 │ ├─ Browser (CDP + managed Chromium – full web control)
 │ ├─ Canvas (A2UI agent-driven visual workspace)
 │ ├─ Node actions (camera live feed, screen record, notify popups, location pings…)
 │ ├─ Cron / webhooks / session juggling
 │ └─ Skills (ClawHub registry – community poison or power)
 │
 └─→ LLMs (Claude Opus preferred, OpenAI backup, local LLMs, automatic failover)

A message arrives through any channel and gets routed to the Gateway. The Gateway decides what needs to happen next, then wakes the Pi/RPC agent or main agent. The agent uses tools and LLMs to process everything and sends the response back through the same path. It stays entirely local unless you deliberately configure remote access, which is the biggest gotcha — you will see later in the article.

item.title: Vectors in Linear Algebra: A Simple Guide with Real-World Examples
item.description:
What Exactly Are Vectors?

Imagine an arrow, it shows you both a direction it is going in and how far it will move in that direction. This arrow is what we call a vector!

The vector essentially is comprised of:

  • Length (also called magnitude or size)
  • Direction (which way it’s pointing)

You’re thinking sure it looks like a bunch of mathematics, what does that have to do with me living my life? There are real-life situations that these vectors represent. One such example that most people recognize is Maps.

item.title: From Online Profile Paranoia to AI Complacency: Have We Really Stopped Caring About Privacy?
item.description:
Hey there!!

Let’s chat about something that’s been on my mind a lot lately. Remember the days when we were all up in arms about how much the internet and big tech companies knew about us?

Our entire lives seemed to be online, from search histories, to locations, to all our shopping habits. That was the time we couldn’t stop talking about all the scary data breaches, the creepy targeted ads, and the surveillance fears.

item.title: About
item.description:
Hi, I’m Farah 🔥

I build production infrastructure for agent systems — cloud, distributed systems, scalable backends, and the governance layer that keeps autonomous agents from doing something dumb at 3am.

I’ve spent time at Microsoft and X (formerly Twitter), shipping through some of the most chaotic engineering environments in the industry. Before that: a Computer Science degree earned the hard way, and years volunteering to bring tech education to kids who didn’t have easy access to it.
